proposition: The Mafāḥiṣ takes as its focus the form of the letters that admits no admixture of conventional meaning, and contrasts this with the mixed approach of Ghazālī, Ibn Sīnā and of Ibn Turka's own grandfather Ṣadr al-Dīn Turka and elder brother Ṣadr al-Dīn.

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, paraphrasing or translating Ibn Turka's own work
mediation.note: Melvin-Koushki cites section 2.6 of the Mafāḥiṣ; the section is translated later in the dissertation, not opened
